body: Experimental marking landed in #1902 (ADR-0049): this property is now flagged `[EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced]` in the spec so authors aren't misled. **This issue stays open** to track the actual enforcement (or removal with the feature) at M2 — the marking only neutralised the false promise, it did not implement the behaviour.

Resolved by #2302 (squash-merged to \`main\` as 6c4fbd993).

**ENFORCE.** The platform expresses elevated identity via the ObjectQL \`options.context\` (\`{ isSystem: true }\` bypasses RLS; \`{ userId, roles, … }\` scopes it), so \`runAs\` is enforced rather than removed.

Root cause: the CRUD nodes passed **no identity at all** to ObjectQL, so the security middleware was skipped entirely — every flow ran effectively elevated regardless of \`runAs\`.

The fix:
- The engine establishes the run's data-layer identity from \`flow.runAs\` at setup (on a context **copy**, so the caller's context is restored afterward) and persists it on suspend so \`resume()\` re-establishes it.
- Every CRUD node passes \`options.context\` via \`resolveRunDataContext\`: \`system\` → \`{ isSystem: true }\` (elevated, RLS-bypassing); \`user\` (default) → the triggering user \`{ userId, roles, permissions, tenantId }\` (RLS-respecting; can never exceed the trigger's grants).
- The REST trigger route + record-change trigger now forward the caller's \`roles\`/\`tenantId\`, so \`runAs:'user'\` matches a direct request by that user.
- Removed the \`[EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced]\` marker; \`docs/audits/2026-06-flowschema-property-liveness.md\` marks \`runAs\` live; the spec liveness ledger classifies \`flow/runAs\` as a **proof-backed** high-risk class (ADR-0054).

Proven both directions, RED→GREEN: dogfood gate \`flow-runas.dogfood.test.ts\` (a restricted member triggering system vs user flows on an owner-scoped record) + service-automation unit/regression tests \`crud-runas.test.ts\`.

Behavior change: flows that relied on the implicit elevation now run as the triggering user — declare \`runAs:'system'\` on flows that must exceed the trigger's access. Schedule-triggered runs (no trigger user) under \`user\` stay unscoped; tracked as a follow-up.

Part of the metadata-liveness audit umbrella #1878 (ADR-0049).
